verdict.rationale: Direct word-level searches confirm a dense, recurring planning vocabulary spoken of God as fixed and effective across both Testaments. Acts 2:23 couples the perfect passive participle (a completed action whose result still stands, in the passive form) of 'to mark out' (horizo, G3724) with 'counsel' (boule, G1012) and 'foreknowledge' (prognosis, G4268), and in the same sentence charges the hearers 'you killed' (aneilate). Acts 4:28 names the determined event with 'as many things as' (hosa) plus a divine subject (the verb form 'predetermined' (proorisen) is tagged in the MACULA Greek dataset under 'to foresee' (proorao, G4275), with the parallel sense to 'to predestine' (proorizo), both rendering 'predetermined to happen'). Ephesians 1:11 escalates the scope with the present participle 'working' (energountos) plus 'all things' (ta panta) governed by 'counsel' (boule) and 'will' (thelema). Isaiah 14:24 uses the Hebrew intensive form (Piel) of 'to devise' (damah) plus the simple active form (Qal) of 'to purpose' (yaats) with the Qal of 'will stand' (qum) in the 'just as, so' (kaasher, ken) correspondence, and Isaiah 46:10, Proverbs 19:21, and Job 23:13 repeat 'counsel' (etsah) plus 'will stand' (qum) to say the LORD's counsel stands. The words assert an effective decree but do not themselves rank its EXTENT (all events versus the redemptive purpose) nor specify its relation to the real human agency the same texts affirm, so the verdict is true while the open seam is scope and mode, not existence.

scripture.force: Peter pairs 'the fixed counsel and foreknowledge of God' (te hōrismenē boulē kai prognōsei tou theou; built from 'to mark out' (horizō, G3724) in the perfect passive participle form, that is, a completed action whose result still stands, in the passive form) with the active charge 'you killed' (aneilate) mediated by 'through the hand of lawless men' (dia cheiros anomōn). The dataset confirms 'to mark out' (horizō) here as the perfect passive (V-RPP-DSF), which is the lexically strongest 'fixed and settled' form. Both clauses stand in one sentence with no smoothing connective. 'Foreknowledge' (prognōsis, G4268) occurs only twice in the entire Bible (here and 1 Peter 1:2), so its precise force, prior knowing versus effective pre-determining, cannot be triangulated from usage alone.

The prayer names specific responsible agents (Herod, Pontius Pilate, the Gentiles, the peoples of Israel) as the ones who 'were gathered' (synēchthēsan) against the holy servant Jesus. Named, accountable human actors are catalogued in verse 27 immediately before verse 28 attributes the same event to God's prior determination, so responsibility is asserted as densely as decree.

'To do whatever your hand and your counsel predetermined to happen' (poiēsai hosa hē cheir sou kai hē boulē sou proōrisen genesthai). The infinitive of purpose plus the relative quantifier 'as many things as' (hosa, G3745) plus the aorist active (a completed past action, active form) 'predetermined' (proōrisen) assigns the full set of verse 27 events to God's prior determination, coordinating 'hand' (cheir) and 'counsel' (boulē) as the determining cause. The dataset tags 'predetermined' (proōrisen) under 'to foresee' (proorao, G4275, a single occurrence in the entire Bible) rather than 'to predestine' (proorizo, G4309); standard parsing reads it as the aorist of 'to predestine' (proorizo), and both carry the divine 'predetermine to happen' force, so the verdict does not turn on the lemma split.

Dataset-verified token order: 'to predestine' (proorizō, G4309) in the aorist passive participle form (a completed past action, passive: 'we having been predestined') governs the elect 'we', while a separate clause has 'to work' (energeō, G1754) in the present active participle form (ongoing, active: 'working') with object 'all things' (ta panta; 'all' (pas, G3956) in the accusative plural neuter, which is the direct-object form) 'according to the counsel of his will' (kata tēn boulēn tou thelēmatos autou). The present tense of 'to work' (energeō) signals ongoing operation. The reach to 'whatsoever comes to pass' rests on the 'working all things' (energeō ta panta) clause, not on 'to predestine' (proorizō), which across its 5 occurrences in the entire Bible (Romans 8:29, Romans 8:30, 1 Corinthians 2:7, Ephesians 1:5, Ephesians 1:11) consistently governs salvation-related objects.

Sworn oath formula confirmed by OSHB (Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible) morphology: 'to devise, plan' (damah, H1819) in the Hebrew intensive form (Piel) perfect (completed action) first common singular ('I have devised, planned') and 'to purpose, counsel' (yaats, H3289) in the simple active form (Qal) perfect first common singular ('I have purposed, counseled') paired with 'to come about' (hayatah, H1961) in the Qal perfect third feminine singular ('it has come about') and 'to stand' (qum, H6965) in the Qal imperfect (ongoing or future) third feminine singular ('it will stand'). The 'just as, so' (kaasher, ken) correspondence asserts one-to-one realization of divine purpose. 'To devise, plan' (damah) carries multiple senses (its dominant Qal sense is 'to resemble'), so the decree weight here rests on the Piel 'devise' sense plus 'to purpose' (yaats), which the construction supplies.

OSHB (Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible)-verified: 'My counsel shall stand and I will do all my pleasure' (atsati taqum vekol chephtsi eeseh). 'Counsel' (etsah, H6098, 'my counsel') plus 'to stand' (qum, H6965) in the Qal imperfect (simple active, ongoing or future) third feminine singular ('will stand') plus 'pleasure, purpose' (chephets, H2656, 'my pleasure or purpose') plus 'to do' (asah, H6213) in the Qal imperfect first common singular ('I will do'). OpenBible links this to Ephesians 1:11 (20 votes) and to Isaiah 14:24 (24 votes). It generalizes the Isaiah 14:24 cadence to all divine pleasure, the strongest scope-extending Old Testament witness for the word cluster.

OSHB (Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible)-verified: 'Many plans are in a man's heart, but the counsel of the LORD, that will stand' (rabbot machashavot belev ish, vaatsat YHWH hi taqum). The wisdom genre sets 'many plans' ('plan' is machashavah, H4284) in a man's heart against the 'counsel' (etsah, H6098) of the LORD that 'will stand' ('to stand', qum, H6965, in the Qal imperfect third feminine singular, the identical verb form as Isaiah 14:24 and 46:10). OpenBible links it to Isaiah 14:24 with 27 votes. It extends the word cluster into the Writings and states the human-plan, divine-counsel pairing in one verse.

OSHB (Open Scriptures Hebrew Bible)-verified dual-agency paradigm in the Torah: 'to devise, intend' (chashav, H2803) in the Qal perfect (simple active, completed) second masculine plural ('you devised') evil plus 'to devise, intend' (chashav, H2803) in the Qal perfect third masculine singular with God as subject ('God devised it') for good, on a single event. One verb, two subjects, one outcome, with human culpability and divine purpose both stated. OpenBible links it to Acts 2:23 (11 votes) and Acts 4:28 (6 votes), grounding the responsibility pole of the proposition in narrative.

MACULA-verified: 'according to what has been determined' (kata to hōrismenon), with 'to mark out' (horizō, G3724) in the perfect passive participle form (a completed action whose result still stands, in the passive form), followed by 'woe' (ouai) to the betrayer. Decree and human guilt in one sentence, mirroring Acts 2:23. OpenBible links it to Acts 2:23 with 11 votes. The same perfect passive 'fixed and settled' form of 'to mark out' (horizō) recurs, confirming the term's stable decree-related sense.

complicating_texts.resolution: The same verse that asserts the decree ('the fixed counsel and foreknowledge', hōrismenē boulē kai prognōsei) also indicts the hearers ('you killed', aneilate). The text softens neither pole. The proposition's qualifier ('consistent with creaturely responsibility') is the word pattern itself, not a gloss imposed on the verse. The dataset confirms 'to mark out' (horizō) here as perfect passive (a completed action whose result still stands, in the passive form), the firmest 'fixed and settled' form available.

Verse 27 names Herod, Pontius Pilate, the Gentiles, and the peoples of Israel as the 'were gathered' (synēchthēsan) subjects before verse 28 attributes the event to God's predetermining hand and counsel. Named, accountable agents are not depersonalized by the decree language.

'All things' (ta panta) is unqualified in the 'to work' (energeō) clause, but 'to predestine' (proorizō, the strict predestination verb) in the same verse governs only the elect 'we', and across its 5 occurrences in the entire Bible 'to predestine' (proorizō) is consistently salvation-related. So the verse asserts comprehensive divine operation through 'working all things' (energeō ta panta) while the predestination verb itself stays focused on salvation. Whether 'all things' (ta panta) means literally all events or all things pertaining to the inheritance is not ranked by the vocabulary, which is the genuine scope seam, but it does not negate the effective-decree reading.

The dataset assigns the dictionary form of 'predetermined' (proōrisen) under 'to foresee' (proorao, G4275) rather than 'to predestine' (proorizo, G4309), a single divergent tag in the entire Bible. This is a dictionary-assignment difference, not a sense difference: both render 'God predetermined the event to happen', and the brief lexicon entry for 'to predestine' (proorizo) cites Acts 4:28 as an instance of 'foreordain'. The verdict does not depend on resolving the tag, so it is noted rather than treated as defeating.

variants.note: Acts 2:23, Acts 4:27-28, and Ephesians 1:11 fall outside the ingested ECM apparatus (the critical edition of New Testament textual variants) window (3 John 1:1 to 1:15), so 'not in ECM scope' is honest for them. No variant unit in the bundle or the dataset touches the decree vocabulary in a verdict-altering way. Isaiah 14:24, Isaiah 46:10, Proverbs 19:21, and Genesis 50:20 are Old Testament, so the ECM apparatus does not apply.

competing_lens_verdicts.rationale: Reads Acts 2:23, Acts 4:27-28, and Genesis 50:20 as a straightforward joining of two truths: divine predetermination and human guilt both stand because the texts assert both in single sentences without ranking them. Ephesians 1:11 'working all things' (energeō ta panta) and Isaiah 46:10 'counsel' (etsah) plus 'will stand' (qum) are taken at full extent. This reading uses every term at its strongest and leaves nothing lexically unaccounted.

Grants that God decrees and that his redemptive purpose stands, but restricts the strict predestination verb 'to predestine' (proorizō) to elective and salvation-related objects, which is exactly its attested distribution (Romans 8:29-30, 1 Corinthians 2:7, Ephesians 1:5, and the 'we' of Ephesians 1:11). On this reading 'whatsoever comes to pass' overreaches, since the universal reach hangs only on the multi-sense 'working all things' (energeō ta panta) clause, which could be bounded to 'all things pertaining to the inheritance' in context. This is a real lexical foothold, not a strawman.

Reads 'foreknowledge' (prognōsis) in Acts 2:23 as knowledge of what creatures would freely do, with the decree consequent on that knowledge. This is lexically permissible because 'foreknowledge' (prognōsis) occurs only twice in the entire Bible and its precise force cannot be triangulated from usage; the gloss 'foreknowledge' is itself neutral between 'prior knowing' and 'effective pre-determining'. It is not lexically required, since in 1 Peter 1:2 and the related verb 'foreknowledge' (prognōsis) sits beside elective acts.

Must re-read Isaiah 14:24 'just as I have devised, so it has come about' (kaasher damah ken hayatah) and Isaiah 46:10 'my counsel shall stand' (atsati taqum), plus Proverbs 19:21 'the counsel of the LORD will stand' (atsat YHWH taqum), as 'if-then' conditional rather than as the settled Qal perfect (simple active completed) plus Qal imperfect (simple active future) of 'standing' they morphologically are. The pattern spread across the whole Bible of an unfailing, already-purposed counsel that 'stands' (qum) is the chief lexical obstacle to this lens, which is why it scores as a denial here rather than a partial reading.

hermeneutics.notes: The proposition states two clauses (an eternal effective decree, and real creaturely responsibility) that the texts place side by side without prose reconciliation. The lenses differ on how to relate them and on the EXTENT of the decree, but all four agree the words assert an effective divine purpose. The unresolved item is scope and mode, which the vocabulary underdetermines, not the existence of the decree.

stem_audit.neutralized_form: God's prior purpose stands behind what occurs in history, while human and angelic agents act with real responsibility and culpability.
stem_audit.notes: The phrase 'whatsoever comes to pass, in a way consistent with creaturely responsibility' is a confessional cadence and encodes both a comprehensive-extent claim and a compatibility claim. The lexical evidence (Acts 2:23, Acts 4:27-28, Ephesians 1:11, Isaiah 14:24, Isaiah 46:10, Proverbs 19:21, Genesis 50:20, Luke 22:22) fits the neutralized form fully and fits the original except that the words do not themselves rank the EXTENT of the decree (all events versus the redemptive purpose); 'to predestine' (proorizō) stays salvation-related in all 5 of its occurrences while only 'working all things' (energeō ta panta) reaches all things. The verdict is rendered on the original stem and holds, because the proposition asks whether such an effective, responsibility-compatible decree is asserted, and the vocabulary asserts it; the open scope question is recorded for transparency, not as a defeater. VERDICT-CHANGED: not applicable here, the original stem verdict stands.

lay_summary: The Bible's vocabulary for God's planning is dense, recurring, and spread across the whole Bible. In Acts 2:23 Peter says Jesus was handed over by God's fixed counsel and foreknowledge, using a 'completed action whose result still stands' form of 'to mark out' (horizo, G3724) together with 'counsel' (boule, G1012) and 'foreknowledge' (prognosis, G4268), and in the same breath tells the crowd they killed him. Acts 4:27-28 names Herod, Pontius Pilate, the Gentiles, and the peoples of Israel as the ones who actually gathered, then says they did whatever God's hand and 'counsel' (boule) had 'predetermined' (proorisen) beforehand to happen. Ephesians 1:11 says God 'works' (energeo) all things, 'ta panta', according to the 'counsel' (boule) of his 'will' (thelema). In the Old Testament Isaiah 14:24, Isaiah 46:10, and Proverbs 19:21 repeat one cadence: as God has purposed, so it will stand, using 'counsel' (etsah) with 'to stand' (qum). Genesis 50:20 shows the responsibility side with one verb 'to devise, intend' (chashav) and two subjects, you devised evil but God devised it for good. So the words clearly assert two things at once, an effective prior purpose and real, accountable human action, and they never explain how the two fit. That dual assertion is exactly what the proposition states, so the verdict is yes, with high confidence, because the word cluster spans law, prophets, writings, gospel, narrative, and letter and the strongest verses pair both clauses in one sentence. Where careful readers diverge is not whether God decrees, but how far it reaches. The strict predestination verb 'to predestine' (proorizo), in all five of its uses, governs salvation and the elect, while the reach to every event hangs on the broader phrase 'God works all things' (energeo ta panta), which the words do not pin down to literally everything versus everything tied to his saving plan. And the word 'foreknowledge' (prognosis) appears only twice, too few times to settle whether it means prior knowing or effective pre-determining. Those are the genuine open seams, and they come from the words themselves, not from any outside frame.
